scope: rounds 68 to 70: three measured negative results and one open lead, after the indexer fusion was registered at 14.287598 tok/s / 69.9922 ms a token

o_projection_transpose.cause: attention.py:1688-1689 lays wo_a out as [groups, o_lora_rank, d] and einsums over d, so the framework materialises a transpose of a constant weight every layer
o_projection_transpose.why_it_looked_safe: a transpose changes no value, so pre-transposing once per module looked exact

measured.contiguous_pretranspose: not bit-identical (3/6 then 5/8), and 212.1 us eager, slower

o_projection_transpose.error_when_it_differs: 1 to 2 of 2048 elements, max abs up to 0.5 on bf16
o_projection_transpose.conclusion: the reduction order on this build is not layout-invariant. Not adopted. Recorded as a new deviation class needing explicit user approval, because it is a different op from the row-norm and narrow-head approvals.

lut_expert_projection.how_decided: the bandwidth driver that answers this had been in the evidence bundle since round 48 titled "written, not run". It was run for the first time, with the accepted v2-n64 library (7dce3e3d) and CANN (bbbda1c0) verified first. The first library found on the box was the v1-n64 build (c896289f) and the hash guard rejected it.

standalone.reading: five more experts cost only about 110 us, so the call is per-call-cost dominated rather than per-expert-byte dominated

two_cautions: the harness same-volume read-only sum reference reports 5.4 GB/s while copy_ over the same volume reports 448.3 GB/s; only the copy is a practical device reference
the standalone numbers are host-bound: the same kernel takes 474.9 us standalone against 101 us a call in the model profile, a 4.7x gap, so the 344.5 us fixed cost is not kernel-internal
lut_expert_projection.conclusion: closes "swap the LUT kernel" as a route to 50 tok/s. The dominant cause is M=1 tile padding - one activation row broadcast across expert groups against a cube unit built for M=16 tiles - which is a property of single-request decode, not of the kernel. A better M=1 kernel may still find 1 to 2 ms.

wo_a_second_item_not_pursued.observation: 138 is exactly the call count of _state_post_pv_kernel and _state_prepare_kernel, so these belong to the sparse-attention state machinery rather than the projection

open_lead_for_a_later_round.why_it_looks_real: each call quantises roughly 10 KB and costs 10.5 us, so the cost is launch overhead, not work. modules.py:203-204 calls quantized_linear(x, w1) and quantized_linear(x, w3) on the SAME x, so one quantisation per MoE call is redundant, and 2 MoE FFNs a layer over 40 layers is about 80 redundant calls a forward, roughly 840 us = 1.2%.
open_lead_for_a_later_round.why_it_is_bit_exact: quantising the same unchanged tensor twice produces the same bytes, so reusing the first result cannot change any value
open_lead_for_a_later_round.the_hazard_that_stops_a_quick_fix: the runtime reuses activation buffers (`_reuse` does slot.copy_(value) in decode_pos.py), so a cache keyed on tensor identity would go stale when a buffer is overwritten. A correct fix dedupes at the call site rather than memoising inside the quantiser.
open_lead_for_a_later_round.why_it_was_not_done_this_round: quantized_linear is the soft/reference path while the device path uses the fused kernel, and the profiler did not capture input shapes for it, so pinning the 322 calls provenance needs a targeted capture first

device_bound_confirmation.consequence: host-side time is overlapped; every remaining gain must be less or faster device work
